text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT — CRITICAL — service=inference-db connections_exhausted. Pager: @maria @aj. PD link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/P12345 · page fired for high error rates (503) on /v1/embeddings :rotating_light:

maria: acked in PD and here. I'm the current infra oncall, taking ownership. Observed huge spike in active DB connections + 5xx from inference-api. Will gather metrics now.

aj: also acked, jumping on zoom if needed. If maria wants to lead mitigation I can handle customer comms and scaling.

pagerduty-bot: [PD] Incident P12345 acknowledged by maria. Escalation level: 1 -> oncall.

support-bot: Heads-up: support queue shows 6 customers reported increased latency/timeouts in the last 10m, highest priority: enterprise-acme (account id: acct_324).

maria: quick snapshot from the API metrics dashboard: error rate for /v1/embeddings spiked from 0.2% -> 6.4% in 5m. Latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 2.4s. DB active_connections ~ 1950 (usual ~300). DB max_connections is 2000. Looks like connection pool exhaustion + long-running queries.

aj: can we throttle embedding traffic or route to a fallback model to reduce DB load?

sarah: pinging-in: I'm on DB team, seeing a backlog on wal sender and many idle in transaction. Likely a set of slow queries from a recent batch job.

maria: steps I'm trying now:
1) Temporarily scale inference-api replicas to reduce queueing
2) Increase DB proxy pool size (pgbouncer) to buy time
3) Identify slow queries / offending app

maria: running scale command:```bash
kubectl scale deployment inference-api -n prod --replicas=12
# output: deployment.apps/inference-api scaled
```

sarah: suggested pgbouncer change: bump pool_size from 100 -> 200 on the read pool. Applying cautious increase now.

maria: applying pgbouncer config tweak via ops runbook:```ini
[databases]
max_client_conn = 10000
pool_size = 200
```

incident-bot: pgbouncer config change deployed by maria (runbook-step-3).

aj: I'm posting a quick status update to the incident channel and support: "We are mitigating a DB connection spike affecting embeddings. Team has increased pooling and scaled API; traffic degraded but should improve in ~10-20m. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause." :thumbsup:

support-bot: Noted. Notifying enterprise-acme account owner and updating support ticket #7891.

maria: quick DB query to see active queries:```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle';
-- result: 1720
SELECT pid, query, state, age(now(), query_start) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY age DESC LIMIT 10;
```
Found multiple long-running SELECTs originating from a scheduled analytics job hitting the embedding tables.

sarah: we can kill a couple of the oldest queries to relieve pressure. I'll target ones older than 5m that are clearly analytics and not user-facing. Proceeding to cancel 3 heavy queries.

sarah: cancelled PIDs 12451, 12476, 12502. Connection counts dropping.

maria: connections down to ~850, error rate beginning to fall. p95 latency down to ~400ms. Good progress.

aj: are we seeing any residual per-customer impact? support-bot said 6 customers earlier.

support-bot: Enterprise-acme saw intermittent 503s for 12 minutes, small startup-dev account reported 4 failures. No chargebacks reported yet.

maria: current plan:
- keep API scaled at 12 replicas for next 30m
- keep pgbouncer pool_size=200 for next 1h, then revert if stable
- block the scheduled analytics job and investigate root cause
- notify PD and support when fully resolved

aj: agree. I'll draft a short customer status message and update PD timeline.

maria: handing primary ownership to aj for comms and post-incident tracking. I'll stay as technical lead for 30m then hand off to carol for overnight oncall.

aj: acknowledged handoff. I'll own the incident channel and postmortem doc.

maria: final technical note before handoff: we observed an unbounded fanout in the analytics job that opened many DB connections simultaneously. Mitigation: limit concurrency in the job and add connection pooling at the app layer.

carol: I'll take overnight oncall once mj finishes — ping me at handoff. (carol here, oncall next shift).

maria: handing to carol at 23:30 PST. Last check: error rate ~0.5%, p95 ~180ms, active_connections ~310. Marking incident downgraded to WARN on PD, leaving in 'investigating' for root cause.

pagerduty-bot: [PD] Incident P12345 status changed: acknowledged -> monitoring. Severity reduced to Major.

aj: I'll create postmortem skeleton and assign owners: root cause -> analytics job concurrency; mitigation -> DB pooling + job changes; timeline -> I'll draft now.

maria: thanks everyone. If anything regresses ping me directly.

carol: noted. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if any regression.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now. Please add follow-up action items to the postmortem doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/incidents/P12345-postmortem
